title: Deity of the Holy Spirit
definition: The deity of the Holy Spirit is the doctrine that the Holy Spirit is fully God, sharing the one divine nature with the Father and the Son.
summary: The Holy Spirit is fully God and worthy of worship, trust, and obedience.
christFocus: Jesus sends the Spirit from the Father, and the Spirit glorifies Christ by applying His saving work to believers.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture identifies the Holy Spirit with God. To lie to the Holy Spirit is to lie to God. The Spirit knows the deep things of God, is present with God's people, gives life, sanctifies, and is named with the Father and the Son.

The deity of the Spirit protects the doctrine of the Trinity and the reality of salvation. The Spirit who applies redemption is not lesser than God; He is God working in believers.

Because the Spirit is fully God, His work is powerful, holy, wise, and trustworthy. He does not merely assist from a distance; He dwells in believers and brings the life of God to them.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: If the Spirit is treated as less than God, His work is minimized and Christian life becomes dependent on human strength. This doctrine gives confidence that the One who indwells believers is truly divine.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Depend on the Holy Spirit as God present with you. Do not reduce Christian growth to self-effort. Pray for His help, obey His conviction, and worship the triune God with reverence.
